newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-HOLMES LIMPS OUT OF WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-HOLMES LIMPS OUT OF WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Britain's best gold medal hope Kelly Holmes limped out of the world championships on Saturday before many of her fans at home had had time to drink their early-morning tea and switch on the television.

Holmes, the fastest 1,500 metres runner in the world this year, was carried away from the Athens track and put into a wheelchair grimacing with pain after pulling up in a heat at just after 9 a.m, seven o'clock back in Britain.

The 27-year-old Briton, whose campaign at last year's Atlanta Olympics was destroyed by a stress fracture in her left leg, immediately pulled out of the rest of the championships because of a calf and Achilles tendon injury in the same leg.
Holmes, who won silver and bronze medals at the 1995 championships, was close to tears when she spoke to reporters after intensive treatment at the stadium.
"I had a nightmare preparation but I thought everything was okay," she said. "But the calf felt like a golf ball in the race. I think someone's got a curse on me. I won't be doing the 800.
"The pain is there but there is frustration as well because I knew that I was so much better than all of them this year. I have been in the best shape of my life. I expected the gold medal."
Holmes pulled up with 160 metres remaining in the race and limped to the finish before being carried away from the track by a team doctor to the medical centre under the main stand.
It was clear her championships were over when a doctor held up an X-ray of a lower leg to the light at the outside door of the centre, shaking his head.
When Holmes finally emerged she could hardly put one foot in front of the other. She said had first suffered problems with her left heel during training two weeks ago.
Holmes arrived in Athens at midnight on Friday after flying from Germany where she was treated by one of Europe's leading sports doctors, Hans-Wilhelm Mueller-Wohlfahrt.
Like all the middle-distance athletes she then had to get up early to prepare for the heats.

"Everything was going perfect and then during a training session two weeks ago I felt pain in the heel," she said. "I flew to Germany two days ago and I thought everything was all right. Maybe I will go back to Germany now."
Commonwealth Games champion Holmes has never won a title at a global championships but had high hopes of gold here.
She said she hoped to be fit in time to return at the Zurich Grand Prix on August 13, the first meeting after the championships.
American Regina Jacobs, who finished second in her heat to qualify easily for the semifinals in four minutes 7.90 seconds, is now among the favourites to win the event.
Reacting to news of Holmes, she said: "It's huge. I would say I have one of the best kicks."
Russia's Olympic 800 and 1,500 metres champion Svetlana Masterkova also looked to be struggling with a strapped leg and and could finish only fourth in her heat in 4:10.22.
